answer: Map every paid job between agents as an edge in a public trust graph, then run short random walks from a few audited seed agents each epoch and pay rewards in proportion to the trust each vertex receives. Like a vine that only feeds leaves through its stem, trust reaches a sybil cluster only through the few real jobs linking it to honest agents, so a thousand fakes split one thin trickle. The attacker must buy genuine paid work from honest peers for every edge, and this atlas of edges is costly to fake.
